label: First Vatican Council, Dei Filius Ch. 3…: God joined external arguments to his revelation, divine…
locator: ch. 3, para. 2: voluit Deus cum internis Spiritus Sancti auxiliis externa iungi revelationis suae argumenta
interpretation: So that the obedience of faith be 'rationi consentaneum', God willed to join external arguments of his revelation to the internal helps of the Spirit: divine facts, above all miracles and prophecies, which, since they clearly show God's omnipotence and infinite knowledge, are 'divinae revelationis signa ... certissima et omnium intelligentiae accommodata'. Read as an actual claim about God's revelation, not as the modal stage-3 premise that whatever is God can make a revelation recognizable: the stage-3 statement is general and modal, this one is about the revelation that occurred. The appeal to Moses, the prophets, Christ and the apostles (Mk 16:20, 2 Pet 1:19) is illustration, not a separate claim here.
